flash_696104.description:
Syria's Border Crossings and Customs Authority announced the closure of the Nasib border crossing with Jordan following a Jordanian strike in southern Syria.

The authority said that passenger and cargo traffic through the crossing had been suspended in both directions.

flash_696103.description: Trump defends the war against Iran, warning that Tehran's missiles could threaten US cities: It should’ve been done a long time ago.

flash_696101.description: Israeli actress Gal Gadot receives an honorary doctorate from Bar-Ilan University, reflecting on October 7, Jewish unity and mutual responsibility while urging Israelis to vote.

flash_696099.description: President Trump denies reports that Netanyahu sought another endorsement ahead of Israel's election, while praising the Prime Minister's leadership and their joint actions against Iran.

flash_696131.description:
Noam LeYisrael Party Chairman MK Avi Maoz cast his ballot at a polling station near his home in Jerusalem's Jewish Quarter. After voting, Maoz addressed what he described as a campaign being waged against his party, warning that it was expected to intensify throughout the day.

"Against the backdrop of the fake news campaign that has gained momentum over the past week, and based on information in our possession, we know that it is set to intensify further throughout the day," Maoz said.

He urged the public to ignore the "background noise" and emphasized: "Noam LeYisrael is staying in the race until the very end, and with God's help, we will be the surprise of the elections. Together, we will bring victory for Jewish education in the Jewish state."

flash_696130.description:
The Yisrael Beytenu Party has reported suspected election irregularities at polling station No. 45, located at 10 Gamla Street in Kiryat Ono. According to information received by the party, Yisrael Beytenu ballot slips, marked with the Hebrew letter Lamed (ל), have not been available at the polling station since it opened this morning.

Following the report, Yisrael Beytenu appealed to the Central Elections Committee, demanding that it investigate the incident and ensure the right of all voters to cast their ballots freely and equally.

flash_696128.description: President Isaac Herzog and First Lady Michal vote in Jerusalem, celebrating Israeli democracy and expressing hope for an Election Day free of disruptions.

flash_696126.description:
Asher Siman Tov, 103, who immigrated to Israel from Afghanistan and is one of the elders of the Orot HaTorah community in Bat Yam, arrived at a polling station this morning to exercise his democratic right to vote.

Siman Tov, who was able to participate in the elections even at his advanced age, voted for the Religious Zionist Party, placing a ballot marked with the Hebrew letter Tet (ט) in the ballot box.

Asher Siman Tov votes at 103Courtesy

flash_696123.description:
Shas Chairman Aryeh Deri warned of high voter turnout among left-wing and Arab voters, claiming that tens of thousands of Israelis had traveled from abroad specifically to participate in the elections and bring down the government.

"Unfortunately, voter turnout among the left and the Arabs is very high. Tens of thousands have arrived from abroad to vote and bring down the rule of the Torah," Deri said.

He added that, in light of the situation, "We must do everything possible to strengthen our position."

flash_696122.description:
Yashar Party Chairman Gadi Eisenkot began Election Day this morning at a polling station in Ofakim, alongside Shirel Hogeg, a local resident running on his party's slate.

"Today, we are embarking on a new path, with a shared future of healing and rebuilding. I call on everyone to vote for 'Derech' so that we will have the power to bring about change and a better future for all Israeli citizens," he said.

Later today, Eisenkot is expected to visit a polling station at Kibbutz Nir Oz, together with kibbutz member and former hostage Gadi Moses.

flash_696120.description: The NYPD is negotiating a $750,500 deal for Israeli-made AI phone-tracking technology, sparking privacy concerns.

flash_696118.description:
The Together Party filed a complaint with the Central Elections Committee, alleging that Likud representatives at polling stations are tracking voters and reporting information about them through an app, in violation of the law and the committee's guidelines.

The complaint was filed following documentation recorded by an election inspector in the Southern Sharon region, which the party claims provides evidence of this conduct.

flash_696116.description: Israel's Sephardic Chief Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef exercised his democratic right on Tuesday morning and cast his vote in Jerusalem.

flash_696114.description:
Polling stations across Israel are opening this morning for the elections to the 26th Knesset. Most polling stations will be open from 7:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m.

In small communities and at polling stations located in hospitals, prisons, and nursing homes, voting will end earlier, at 8:00 p.m.

flash_696112.description: Netanyahu reportedly sought rabbis' help to persuade Ofer Winter to withdraw from the election. Rabbi David Abuhatzeira instead supports his candidacy.

flash_696110.description: The Justice Department files a new criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey over an alleged 2016 leak, triggering a dispute over filing deadlines.

flash_696108.description: Intel is acquiring Israeli quantum software company Classiq for $2.3 billion, marking a record deal for the industry and a milestone for Israel's technology sector.

flash_696106.description:
Syrian authorities reported that eight people, including three children, were killed in Jordanian airstrikes in the southern part of the country.

A Syrian health official said that four other people were wounded in the strikes.

flash_696102.description: Ambassador Danny Danon confronts UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese over her accusations against Israel and presents her with a resignation letter to sign: You are a disgrace to the UN.

flash_696181.description:
0:00 /
1x
תיעוד חריג: מכות ליד קלפי ברהטלפי סעיף 27א

flash_696180.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich have just spoken and agreed to coordinate a joint effort to drive right-wing voters to the polls in the evening hours.

The conversation took place against the backdrop of the voting percentages in the Arab sector, which were described as worrying.

flash_696178.description: Amid long lines at polling stations, Israel's Central Elections Committee allows expired IDs and orders faster voting procedures and priority for disabled voters.

flash_696176.description: Channel 12's Amit Segal reports strong participation in Arab, center-left, and Likud strongholds.

flash_696174.description: 'Together' chairman Naftali Bennett, who attained control of Prime Minister's Office with just six Knesset seats in 2021, warns Israelis that party size does not matter - only bloc size matters.

flash_696172.description: IDF voter turnout by 1:00 p.m. at 48%

flash_696170.description:
The Central Elections Committee clarified that election officials may begin verifying the identity of the next voter in line while the current voter is behind the voting booth curtain casting their ballot, in an effort to reduce waiting times at polling stations.

The Director General of the Central Elections Committee warned: "Any polling station secretary who fails to prevent overcrowding will be dismissed from their position."

flash_696169.description:
Political commentator Amit Segal addressed the high voter turnout in strongholds of the Southern Faction of the Islamic Movement, arguing that it was the result of Mansour Abbas's early preparations for the elections. According to Segal, voter turnout in these strongholds is among the highest in the country.

Segal noted that the phenomenon is unusual even by international standards, with the poorest segment of society recording exceptionally high voter turnout. He added that, as of the time of his report, turnout in these areas was even higher than in the Haredi sector.

flash_696167.description: Security guards stop man approaching Democrats chairman Yair Golan, knife falls from suspect's clothing.

flash_696165.description:
Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg issued an interim order today prohibiting the United Torah Judaism faction and its representatives at polling stations from reporting the number of voters who have cast their ballots in real time.

The order was issued in response to a petition filed by the Movement for Quality Government in Israel against United Torah Judaism. The judge ordered the faction to submit its response by 2:15 p.m.

flash_696164.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, cast their ballots at a Jerusalem polling station

"This is a fateful moment; we know what is at stake. Vote for the future of the State of Israel," Netanyahu stated.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu votes in Israeli elections

flash_696163.description:
According to the latest voting figures, voter turnout stands at 28.6% in Tel Aviv, 26.8% in Jerusalem, and 26.6% in Haifa.

Among Israel's three largest cities, Tel Aviv leads in voter turnout, followed by Jerusalem and Haifa.

flash_696162.description: Ruby Chen, father of fallen soldier Itay Chen, is called a 'traitor' outside a Netanya polling station while urging Israelis to remember the fallen.

flash_696161.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog visits Central Elections Committee on Election Day, chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg wishes Israel 'great success.'

flash_696160.description: Acting Elections Committee Director: If lines continue past 10 p.m., voting will remain open

flash_696159.description: The word “choice," is not limited to the ballot box.

flash_696157.description: An Egyptian national who crossed into Israel near Nitzana is suspected of planning a terror attack; Shin Bet investigators identify possible nationalist motives.

flash_696155.description: Netherlands reverses its decision to return to Eurovision after Dutch broadcasters refuse to support participation alongside Israel.

flash_696153.description: Police arrest three Negev residents suspected of offering cash in exchange for votes for Ra'am in the Knesset elections.

flash_696206.description: Voter turnout figures as of 8:00 p.m. reveal significant differences between communities in Judea and Samaria.

flash_696205.description: Conservative commentator Mark Levin urges Likud and coalition supporters to get out and vote, warning that low turnout could put Israel's future and security at risk.

flash_696204.description: After a turbulent election day, the political drama reaches its climax: TV exit polls reveal the emerging distribution of Knesset seats and the balance of power between the political blocs.

flash_696202.description: Following a request by Likud, joined by Shas and Otzma Yehudit, the Central Elections Committee's presidium decided not to extend voting hours.

flash_696200.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s presidential election, has left the country for the US. Brazilian federal police are investigating, while Argentina denies he entered the country.

flash_696198.description:
The he Central Elections Committee decided to reject the request to extend voting hours at polling stations.

In accordance with the decision, the polling stations will close at 10:00 PM as planned, despite requests submitted by Likud and other parties due to congestion, long lines, and poor weather.

flash_696196.description: Media in Qatar, Lebanon, and Turkey focus on Arab voter turnout in Israel’s elections, while questioning whether a new government would change Israeli policy.

flash_696194.description: Polls open across Israel as 7.3 million eligible voters choose the next Knesset, with exit polls expected at 10 p.m. and a close race potentially ahead.

flash_696192.description: The IDF reports that as of 5:00 PM, the voting rate among those serving in the IDF stands at 68%, compared to 65% at the same time in the elections for the 25th Knesset.

flash_696190.description: Shas and United Torah Judaism campaign headquarters fear a loss of strength amid high voter turnout nationwide and are activating emergency operations to get voters to the polls.

flash_696188.description: Zehut leader Moshe Feiglin warns of a wide turnout gap between Arab voters and the national camp, urging eligible English speakers to vote to ensure national camp leadership.

flash_696186.description: Elections Committee Deputy Director General: Voter turnout may break 80% record

flash_696184.description: New York State Governor Kathy Hochul claims she is doing her best to protect Jewish New Yorkers and blames Netanyahu for the wave of antisemitism on Israel's election day.

flash_696182.description: Pollster Shlomo Filber predicts that unusually high voter turnout will make it harder for small parties to cross the electoral threshold.

flash_696179.description:
The Central Elections Committee clarified that a voter who encounters a damaged ballot should contact the polling clerk to receive a proper ballot.

In the event that a note from the requested list is missing, a white note can be used and the letters of the list can only be written on it in blue ink.

flash_696233.description:
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot addressed senior officials in Israel's defense establishment and civil service, claiming that "Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister without a mandate or public trust."

Eisenkot urged senior officials to resist political pressure, stating, "Remember that you serve the state and the interests of Israel's citizens alone. You have my unequivocal backing."

Addressing Netanyahu directly, he declared, "Don't you dare use Israel's security for your political purposes."

flash_696232.description: Eisenkot: We made history, the public has voted against Netanyahu remaining in office

flash_696230.description: Channel 13 News released an updated election exit poll showing Likud gaining two seats to reach 27, while Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party loses one seat, dropping to 22.

flash_696229.description:
Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett responded to the election exit poll results, declaring, "People of Israel, hold your heads high. The alliance of those who serve has defeated the draft evaders."

Bennett added that "the October 7 government will be sent packing," expressing confidence that the current government would be replaced.

flash_696227.description: Religious Zionist Party chairman greeted with dancing at party headquarters, expresses hope that soldiers' votes would boost his party, and vows to continue Jewish settlement in Judea and Samaria and Gaza.

flash_696225.description: According to an updated election exit poll released by Channel 14, the right-wing bloc has increased its projected total to 62 Knesset seats.

flash_696223.description:
Otzma Yehudit chairman and Minister Itamar Ben Gvir responded to the exit poll results, warning against the formation of a unity government with Gadi Eisenkot. "This is exactly the scenario we warned against. It would be a terrible mistake," he said.

Ben Gvir expressed pride in his party's achievements and the support of hundreds of thousands of voters, adding, "I didn't enter politics to apologize for my principles, and I didn't come here to abandon the path I believe in."

flash_696222.description: Following disappointing exit polls, Winter vows to continue his political journey and rejects claims of wasted votes.

flash_696220.description: Liberman: There needs to be a revolt in the Likud, oust Netanyahu

flash_696218.description: The electoral threshold in the elections for the 26th Knesset was particularly high, requiring parties to receive approximately 186,000 votes to secure representation in the Knesset.

flash_696217.description: Eisenkot declares victory for the Zionist majority, Lapid speaks of a collapse, and Golan hails a historic opportunity. Zohar warns against a government backed by Arab parties.

flash_696215.description: Ofer Winter is expected to deliver a statement this evening at 11:25 p.m., following the release of exit polls for the 26th Knesset elections.

flash_696213.description: Kan 11 exit poll update: Bennett drops to 13 seats, while the Joint List rises to 11

flash_696211.description: Amit Segal outlines three possible scenarios following the exit poll results: a minority government, a unity government, or another election, saying that even a single Knesset seat could change the options for forming a government.

flash_696209.description:
According to the i24NEWS exit poll conducted by pollster Tzuriel Sharon, Likud leads with 27 seats, the Yashar Party receives 20 seats, and the Beyachad Party wins 15.

Yair Golan's party and the Joint List each receive 9 seats, Shas wins 8, and United Torah Judaism, Ra'am, and Otzma Yehudit each receive 7 seats.

Religious Zionism receives 6 seats, while Yisrael Beytenu wins 5 seats.

flash_696208.description:
According to Mano Geva's exit poll for Channel 12 News, Likud wins 24 seats, the Yashar Party 22, Bennett 12, the Joint List 11, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu 9 each, Shas 8, Ra'am 7, and United Torah Judaism, Ben Gvir's party, and Religious Zionism 6 seats each.

The parties led by Hendel, Zelekha, and Winter fail to cross the electoral threshold.

According to the exit poll, the Change Bloc stands at 52 seats, Netanyahu's bloc at 50 seats, and the Arab parties at 18 seats.

flash_696252.description:
According to partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, with approximately 37.4% of the votes counted, the current coalition drops to 57 seats, the change bloc rises to 47, and the Arab parties increase their combined representation to 16 seats. Likud loses one seat, falling to 28, while Yashar rises to 21 and the Joint List climbs to 12.

Together receives 11 seats, United Torah Judaism and Yisrael Beytenu eight each, while the Democrats, Otzma Yehudit, Shas, and the joint Religious Zionism-Zehut list each receive seven. Ra'am remains above the electoral threshold with 3.81% of the vote, giving it four seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.72% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.77%. These are partial results and may change as vote counting continues.

flash_696251.description: Minister Amichai Chikli criticizes those who predicted just 18 seats for Likud but stresses that it is still too early to declare an election victory.

flash_696250.description: Likud spokesman Guy Levy tells Arutz Sheva-Israel National News that exit polls point to a significant achievement for Netanyahu, but stresses that victory is not yet certain.

flash_696248.description:
According to the partial official results updated at 5:03 a.m., with approximately 31.2% of the votes counted, the distribution of political blocs remains unchanged: the current coalition holds 59 seats, the change bloc 46, and the Arab parties 15. Ra'am remains above the electoral threshold with 3.7% of the vote, giving it four seats.

In the distribution of seats, Likud leads with 29, followed by Yashar with 20, the Joint List and Together with 11 each, United Torah Judaism with nine, and Yisrael Beytenu with eight. Otzma Yehudit, the Democrats, Shas, and the joint Religious Zionism-Zehut list each receive seven seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.72% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.8%.

These are partial results and may change as vote counting continues.

flash_696247.description: With 28.2% of votes counted: Coalition drops to 59 seats, Ra'am crosses electoral threshold

flash_696246.description: Matan Kahana tells Arutz Sheva-Israel National News that Netanyahu's political career is over and makes clear that Yashar will not form a government dependent on Arab parties.

flash_696244.description: According to The Wall Street Journal, the US has warned Gulf Arab nations of a possible military offensive against Iran after the midterms.

flash_696242.description: The Central Elections Committee has begun releasing the official results of Israel's 26th Knesset elections. The figures are being updated as vote counting progresses.

flash_696240.description: Netanyahu: Thanks to our heroic soldiers, we have achieved wonders that changed the Middle East

flash_696238.description: Netanyahu takes the stage to deliver speech at Jerusalem Convention Center

flash_696236.description: According to the latest update to Channel 12 News' exit poll for Israel's 26th Knesset elections, Netanyahu's bloc has strengthened to 52 seats, while Eisenkot's bloc is projected to win 49 seats. The Arab parties are projected to receive 19 seats.

flash_696235.description: Zehut chairman warns of growing Arab party influence, presents his party as the answer to Israel's identity crisis, and sets his sights on the Defense Ministry.

flash_696231.description: Geffen Brailovsky, head of Amcha Yisrael's youth campaign, tells Arutz Sheva-Israel National News she believes the official election results will tell a different story.

flash_696228.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to arrive at the International Convention Center in Jerusalem in approximately an hour to deliver a speech following the release of the election exit polls and the start of the official vote count.

flash_696226.description:
The Central Elections Committee announced that the first official results of the elections for the 26th Knesset have begun to be released.

The results will be updated throughout the night as vote counting and verification progress. The committee emphasized that the figures are preliminary and partial and may change.

flash_696224.description:
Channel 14 released an updated election exit poll showing that Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu party would fail to cross the electoral threshold.

As a result, Netanyahu's bloc has risen to 61 seats, securing a majority sufficient to form a government, according to the updated exit poll.

flash_696275.description: Judges question the prosecution's attempt to limit Mandelblit's cross-examination, raising concerns over investigative actions and possible abuse of process.

flash_696274.description: Partial official results updated at 12:32 p.m. with approximately 77.6% of the votes counted: Change bloc gains two seats since the previous update, rising to 49 seats. Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar rose to 22 seats, and Naftali Bennett's Together party rose to 12, while the Joint List dropped to 11 and Yisrael Beytenu dropped to seven.

flash_696272.description: United Torah Judaism leaders celebrate reported election gains, reject coalition talks until final results, and vow to defend haredi rights.

flash_696270.description: United Torah Judaism demands law exempting yeshiva students from military service, refusing to aid coalition until law is passed

flash_696268.description: According to partial official results of Israel's 26th Knesset elections, updated at 10:50 a.m. on Wednesday, with approximately 70.7% of the votes counted, the coalition bloc remains at 54 seats, while the change bloc loses a seat, dropping to 47. The Joint List gained a seat from 12 to 13, at the expense of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party which has dropped to 20 seats. Ra'am remains at six seats.

flash_696266.description: An archaeological reminder that this is a Jewish state by right, no matter what the Arab parties' ambitions are. Opinion.

flash_696264.description:
As of 9:44 a.m. on Wednesday, with approximately 66.3% of the votes counted the coalition bloc has fallen from 56 to 54 seats, while the change bloc remains at 48. The Joint List receives 12 seats, while Ra'am rises from four to six.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party loses one seat, falling from 28 to 27, but remains the largest party. Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party maintains its strength with 21 seats. The Joint List remains at 12 seats, while Naftali Bennett's Together party receives 11. The Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu each receive eight seats. United Torah Judaism loses another seat, falling from eight to seven. Itamar Ben Gvir's Otzma Yehudit remains at seven seats, as does Shas. The joint Religious Zionist-Zehut list maintains six seats.

flash_696263.description: The Central Elections Committee has begun releasing the official results of Israel's 26th Knesset elections. The figures are being updated as vote counting progresses.

flash_696261.description:
According to partial results updated at 9:09 a.m. on Wednesday, with approximately 60.2% of the votes counted, the current coalition bloc has strengthened to 56 seats, while the change bloc has fallen to 48 seats.

The seat distribution by party:

Likud - 28

Yashar - 21

Joint List - 11

Together - 11

Democrats - 8

United Torah Judaism - 8

Yisrael Beytenu - 8

Otzma Yehudit - 7

Shas - 7

Religious Zionist Party-Zehut - 6

Ra'am - 4

Reservists-Economic Party - Below threshold (2.67%)

Amcha Yisrael - Below threshold (1.64%)

flash_696260.description: Three Hamas Nukhba terrorists eliminated in Gaza, including one who abducted Israelis from Kibbutz Nir Oz on October 7 and later helped hold hostages, including Nimrod Cohen.

flash_696259.description: Terrorist armed with two knives charges security guard at Israeli embassy in Serbia.

flash_696257.description: Channel 12 analyst Amit Segal criticizes pollsters for 'years' of inaccurate polling, says no statistical explanation for discrepancies.

flash_696255.description:
According to the partial official results updated at 7:19 a.m., with approximately 48.4% of the votes counted, the current coalition holds 57 seats, the change bloc 47, and the Arab parties 16.

Likud receives 28 seats, followed by Yashar with 21. The Together Party and the Joint List receive 11 seats each, followed by the Democrats with nine, United Torah Judaism and Yisrael Beytenu with eight each, Shas and Otzma Yehudit with seven each, and the Religious Zionist Party-Zehut alliance with six. Ra'am is currently above the electoral threshold with 3.41% of the vote, securing four seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.66% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.67%.

flash_696254.description: The US will grant visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family after his election defeat in Brazil, as questions surround his departure amid a passport surrender order.

flash_696253.description:
US President Donald Trump commented on the elections in Israel in a post on Truth Social.

“When President Trump endorsed Bibi Netanyahu, the whole tide turned, and now, rather than a decisive defeat for a Great Prime Minister, it looks like a big come-from-behind stalemate, or even a WIN for Netanyahu. It all took place AFTER the Endorsement by President Trump, who only wants what is good for the Middle East, Israel, and the United States of America!" he wrote.

flash_696249.description: Trump says he would attack Iran again without hesitation and insists he will decide when the war ends, demanding guarantees that Tehran will never obtain nuclear weapons.

flash_696294.description: Hillel Fuld, brother of terror victim Ari Fuld, has accused Osama Saadi, a lawyer and member of the Joint List, of representing the Palestinian Authority in a lawsuit over its payments to the family of his brother’s killer.

flash_696293.description: After his party failed to cross the electoral threshold, Ofer Winter addresses the defeat, accepts personal responsibility, but emphasizes that he will not abandon his public activities.

flash_696291.description: The Likud Party alleges serious irregularities at polling stations in the Arab sector and is demanding that the police and Shin Bet investigate evidence it intends to submit.

flash_696289.description: The cost of the war in Iran to the US military is estimated at $47 billion, CBS reported, based on an estimate by the US Central Command (CENTCOM). The amount does not include the costs of damage caused to US bases in the Middle East, so the total cost is expected to be higher.

flash_696288.description: Israeli Consul General Ophir Akunis urges political leaders to form a broad unity government following the Knesset elections, stressing the importance of national unity for Israel, Diaspora Jewry, and the country's security.

flash_696287.description: A Spokesperson for the European Union issued the following statement following yesterday's Knesset elections in Israel: "The European Union congratulates the Israeli people on yesterday’s elections, which saw a high voter turnout, reflecting Israel’s vibrant democracy. There now begins a period of political negotiations to form the next Israeli government. The EU looks forward to engaging with the next government on the basis of our longstanding relationship and commitment to democratic principles and common values, as well as to further advancing people-to-people contacts. The EU approach will continue to be based on a frank and open dialogue in view of advancing our bilateral cooperation, addressing all issues of concern and working together to promote regional stability, security, and a just and lasting peace."

flash_696286.description: The change shows a shift in the balance of power among the haredi parties, with the UTJ party pulling ahead by tens of thousands of votes.

flash_696285.description: President Isaac Herzog welcomed the high voter turnout, announced that consultations on forming a government would begin next week, and called on political parties to prevent another election.

flash_696284.description: Netanyahu blasts Joint List after MK Osama Saadi accuses Israel of genocide and ethnic cleansing, warns 'bloc of change' seeking to form government with Arab parties.

flash_696283.description: Despite Jonathan Pollard's backing and an alliance with Aleh Yarok, Sharren Haskel's party receives just 804 votes, trailing two fringe parties.

flash_696282.description: The question is not merely whether we remain attached to the people who taught us Torah. It is whether we continue to follow the derech they showed us.

flash_696281.description: The question is not merely whether we remain attached to the people who taught us Torah. It is whether we continue to follow the derech they showed us.

flash_696280.description: Three Hamas commanders eliminated in Gaza strikes, including two who infiltrated Israel during the October 7 massacre.

flash_696279.description: What does the Akeidah, the binding of Yitzchak, have to do with Gaza?

flash_696278.description: What does the land of Moriah mean?

flash_696277.description: Jewish treasures stolen by Nazis 88 years ago come home, thanks to Arizona synagogue.

flash_696276.description: Opposition leaders aim to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana when new Knesset is sworn in, even without majority needed to form government.

flash_696273.description: Two high-speed trains collide near Toledo, Spain, causing numerous casualties and suspension of rail service.

flash_696271.description: With over 70% of votes counted, UTJ leads Shas by over 23,446 votes, potentially ending the Sephardic-haredi party's dominance as the largest haredi party.

flash_696269.description: Macron cannot fight what he refuses to remember. Opinion.

flash_696267.description: Unless Democrats succeed in rigging the upcoming midterm elections, Americans will continue to benefit and prosper from the POTUS’s heroic vision. Look at what he accomplished in two years. Opinion.

flash_696265.description: Democrats chairman Yair Golan claims Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost elections, urges formation of center-left government with Arab parties.

flash_696309.description: Avigdor Liberman is reportedly ignoring calls from Bennett and Eisenkot, doubts the feasibility of replacing the Knesset Speaker, and prefers to wait for developments.

flash_696308.description: United Torah Judaism gained some 40,000 votes but was held back by high nationwide turnout, while smaller parties left nearly 200,000 votes without representation.

flash_696307.description:
According to partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, updated at 11:23 p.m., with approximately 90% of the votes counted, the current coalition holds 53 seats, the opposition bloc 48, and the Arab parties 19.

Likud leads with 26 seats, followed by Yashar with 21. The Joint List and Together each receive 12 seats. The Democrats receive eight seats, while Ra'am, Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, and Shas each receive seven. The joint Religious Zionist-Zehut list receives six seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.63% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.6%.

flash_696305.description: After Shas dropped to seven Knesset seats, four fewer than in the previous elections, calls are emerging within the party to replace chairman Aryeh Deri.

flash_696302.description: The bloc opposed to Netanyahu is considering a move to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana in just two weeks, with Yair Lapid emerging as one of the leading candidates for the position.

flash_696300.description: According to the partial official results, Likud has 26 seats, Yashar 21, Netanyahu's bloc 53, and the opposition bloc 48. Double-envelope ballots are being counted separately.

flash_696298.description: Counting of 'double envelope' votes to begin at 1 am

flash_696296.description: Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu, chief rabbi of Tzfat, has issued a sharp warning against cooperating with the Joint List.

flash_696292.description: A former federal judge shows how Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) could face criminal charges and potentially lose her U.S. citizenship if federal investigators establish that she committed immigration fraud.

flash_696290.description: A left-wing government with the haredi parties? A left-wing government with the Arab parties? A unity government despite promises to boycott Netanyahu?

flash_696319.description: Saudi Arabia announced that it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis from Yemen after air raid sirens sounded in the area of Najran, in the southern part of the kingdom.

flash_696318.description: Qatar presents a new proposal to end the Iran war, but Tehran rejects the terms as unacceptable.

flash_696316.description: Flavio Bolsonaro calls himself Brazil's leader after losing to Lula, accusing authorities of political persecution and vowing to lead the opposition from the US.

flash_696314.description:
According to the partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, updated at 1:18 a.m., with approximately 90.4% of the votes counted, the distribution of seats remains unchanged. The current coalition holds 53 seats, the opposition bloc 48, and the Arab parties 19.

Likud leads with 26 seats, followed by Yashar with 21. The Joint List and Together each receive 12 seats, the Democrats eight, while Ra'am, Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, and Shas each receive seven. The joint Religious Zionist-Zehut list receives six seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.63% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.6%.

flash_696313.description:
The Central Elections Committee announced that counting of the votes cast in outer envelopes, also known as double-envelope ballots, began at 1:00 a.m., following the completion of the required intake, scanning, and verification procedures.

As part of the process, the inner ballot envelopes are removed from the outer envelopes and mixed together to ensure that voters' identities cannot be linked to their ballots, preserving the secrecy of the vote. The ballots are then transferred for counting at the counting facility in the Knesset parking lot.

Meanwhile, the committee reported that the processing of results from regular polling stations is continuing. As of 1:00 a.m., results had been received from 11,712 of the 12,018 regular polling stations, where 5,126,759 voters cast their ballots. The remaining polling stations are undergoing routine verification procedures.

flash_696311.description:
According to the partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, updated at 12:44 a.m., with approximately 90.2% of the votes counted, the distribution of seats remains unchanged from the previous update. The current coalition holds 53 seats, the opposition bloc 48, and the Arab parties 19.

Likud continues to lead with 26 seats, followed by Yashar with 21. The Joint List and Together each receive 12 seats, the Democrats eight, while Ra'am, Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, and Shas each receive seven. The joint Religious Zionism-Zehut list receives six seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.63% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.6%.

flash_696306.description: Brig. Gen. (res.) Erez Wiener, chairman of the Bithonistim movement, criticized Gadi Eisenkot for urging security officials to resist political pressure following the release of election exit polls

flash_696304.description:
A short while ago, an interceptor was launched toward a suspicious aerial target identified in the area in which IDF soldiers are operating in southern Lebanon.

No sirens were sounded in accordance with protocol.

flash_696301.description: An Israeli businessman in his 40s was found dead inside a restroom at a restaurant in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with possible poisoning among the lines of investigation into his death.

flash_696299.description: The results of the elections for the 26th Knesset are still being determined, but the timetable for forming the next government is already clear. Here are all the details.

flash_696297.description: Channel 12 political analyst predicts that Netanyahu will first attempt to reunite the right-wing bloc before approaching potential partners outside it, despite the political obstacles.

flash_696295.description: Figures released by the Yesha Council reveal a gap of nearly 12 percentage points between voter turnout in Judea, Samaria, and the Jordan Valley and the national average.

flash_696343.description:
Minister Yitzhak Wasserlauf said in an interview with Kan News on Reshet Bet that Otzma Yehudit received dozens of reports and video recordings on election day alleging irregularities at polling stations, including claims that money was distributed in exchange for votes for Ra’am.

Wasserlauf described a report received from a party activist at the Beit al-Hikma school in Rahat, according to which a sheikh and several other people were sitting outside the polling station. Ra’am envelopes containing money were reportedly seen at the scene, along with people carrying long-barreled firearms.

He said the materials were forwarded to the relevant authorities in real time, and MK Yitzhak Kroizer contacted Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Solberg regarding the matter.

flash_696342.description:
Alexander Blok (Gurvitz), an Israeli and Russian citizen, was extradited from Israel to the US early Thursday morning to face charges of fraud and computer-related offenses, transferring stolen goods, and money laundering.

According to the allegations, Blok exploited a security vulnerability in the Nomad cryptocurrency platform in August 2022 to withdraw tokens worth approximately $2.8 million. He allegedly converted the tokens and transferred the funds between digital wallets to conceal their origin.

Blok was arrested at Ben-Gurion Airport in May 2025 while on his way to Russia. His extradition proceeded after the Supreme Court rejected his appeal, and his subsequent request for a further hearing was also denied.

flash_696340.description:
The Environmental Protection Ministry has identified the African big-headed ant for the first time in the Neve Sha’anan neighborhood of Haifa. The species is considered one of the world’s 100 most harmful invasive species. Reports of its presence in other parts of the city are also being investigated.

The ministry is working with the Haifa Municipality, the Israel Nature and Parks Authority, and Tel Aviv University to expand monitoring efforts and examine pest-control solutions suited to Israeli conditions.

“The public is asked to report any suspected sightings to help map infestation hotspots and prevent the spread of this invasive species," the ministry said.

flash_696338.description: Collapse sends shockwaves through Shas leadership, 'Focusing on the haredi base at the expense of the traditional electorate was a fatal mistake,' admits a senior Shas official.

flash_696336.description: Following Justice Solberg’s order for a Shin Bet probe into suspected foreign funding, questions arise over legal options if election fraud affected the results.

flash_696334.description: One hundred and twenty people. Several centuries of collective trauma. And absolutely nobody listening. Opinion.

flash_696332.description: Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg instructs Shin Bet chief David Zini to investigate suspected elections interference by illegally-funded foreign Arab entities.

flash_696330.description: Sources close to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu considering unity government with Yashar! chair Gadi Eisenkot, potentially excluding haredi parties, report says.

flash_696326.description: Katharina von Schnurbein takes office as Germany's new antisemitism commissioner as incidents reach record levels and Jewish communities face growing threats.

flash_696324.description: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem says Israel's election results will not affect the terror group's campaign against Israel and again rejects demands to disarm.

flash_696322.description: A California woman sues the DMV after officials revoked her personalized license plate referencing "from the river to the sea," citing concerns over violence.

flash_696320.description: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed calls for ending US military aid to other countries, not just Israel.

flash_696317.description:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke by phone with US President Donald Trump, with the two leaders discussing regional and global developments, according to reports in Turkey.

Erdogan told Trump that Turkey was closely monitoring developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen and was working to resolve the issues through diplomatic means.

flash_696374.description: Residents of the Mitzpe Yehoshua outpost on Mount Ebal spotted construction equipment being used to pave a road from Shechem toward the ancient site. The work was halted following a report to the IDF

flash_696373.description: Clashes between haredi protesters and police on Route 4, protester injured by stun grenade

flash_696371.description: Shin Bet says its election probe is based on independently gathered intelligence, rejects speculation, and warns against blaming the entire Arab sector.

flash_696369.description: After receiving 10,000 votes in elections, Moti Leitner takes responsibility for party's election defeat, acknowledges campaign mistakes, and vows to continue fighting for change within haredi society.

flash_696367.description: Shin Bet: Election manipulation probe ongoing, information not from political sources

flash_696365.description: Following the Flydubai security lapse, authorities have decided to revise airline regulations, requiring carriers to submit crew members' details 48 hours before departure.

flash_696363.description:
The Central Elections Committee announced that the counting of double-envelope ballots has been completed.

So far, results from 12,644 polling stations have been entered into the system, totaling 5,589,836 votes. Of these, 5,564,764 are valid votes and 25,072 are invalid.

flash_696361.description:
Following the Flydubai security lapse, authorities have decided to revise the guidelines for airlines, which will now be required to submit their crew members' details 48 hours before departure.

The new guidelines are intended to allow advance screening of crew members and prevent similar incidents from recurring.

flash_696359.description:
Minister of Settlement Orit Strock criticized the Ra'am party and its chairman, Mansour Abbas, claiming that the party is using its political influence to change the Jewish character of the State of Israel.

Strock called for Ra'am to be excluded from any coalition and even barred from running in Knesset elections. Addressing allegations of election funding from Qatar and Turkey, she demanded a Shin Bet investigation, stating: "All of these matters must be thoroughly investigated."

flash_696357.description: According to the partial official results, Likud has 27 seats, Yashar 21, Netanyahu's bloc 53, the opposition bloc with 48 and Arab parties with 19. Reservists and Economic Party remain below electoral threshold, with 2.67%.

flash_696355.description: Culture Minister Miki Zohar says Yashar! chair Gadi Eisenkot's advisers pushing him to break election promises, form government with Arab parties.

flash_696353.description: Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman insists party will only join coalition of Zionist parties without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, ruling out haredim and Arabs.

flash_696351.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog praises Israel's robust democracy, says suspected foreign interference in elections must be fully investigated.

flash_696349.description: Likud calls suspected foreign interference in Israel's elections 'earthquake,' alleging an attempt to buy Arab votes and demanding thorough investigation.

flash_696347.description:
The mayor of Dnipro, Ukraine, reported that at least 13 people were killed when a Russian drone struck a railway station in the city.

According to reports, the drone hit the station area while a passenger train was there. At least five other people were wounded in the attack.

flash_696346.description: Emuna Schreiber, sister of former Hamas hostage Avinatan Or, suffers spinal fractures while fleeing rock attack in Samaria.
